answer: A hydrodynamic tracer protocol curbs Sybil attacks in a riverine pearl mussel monitoring network. Verifiers pulse a rhodamine plume into the stream, checking arrival latencies at sensors beneath a riparian vine canopy to prove discrete physical locations. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of fabricating and submerging dedicated sensor hardware per identity. However, turbulent eddies and seasonal silt distort plume propagation, causing false rejections of legitimate agents.
